title: SHRDLU: A Critical Code Studies Reading
description:
A Critical Code Studies reading of SHRDLU, Terry Winograd's natural-language-understanding program (MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, 1968–70): a static website reading its code, its 1970 demonstration dialogue, its microworld and its critique, and a research bench for reading the SHRDLU source together in the browser. The bench reads each version's MacLisp files with every defined name cross-referenced, runs SHRDLU from a version's own source, collates versions as text and by definition, traces their genealogy, and holds a public catalogue of SHRDLU's implementations. Live at https://critical-code-studies.github.io/SHRDLU/ and https://critical-code-studies.github.io/SHRDLU/research/.

The site's and the bench's own code is under the GNU General Public License v3.0 (the bench's shared code is bench-kit, https://github.com/critical-code-studies/bench-kit). The SHRDLU sources the repository keeps from others (Winograd's distribution, the ITS copies and Swenson's restoration in source/, the Java port, and the published implementation files in research/implementations/files/) stay under whatever terms their holders set, recorded with each.

A Critical Code Studies project co-led by David M. Berry (University of Sussex) and Mark C. Marino (University of Southern California).
